      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/04/un-vote-world-map-mercator-equal-earth-africa</link>
      <description><p>Togo-sponsored resolution called to phase out traditional map that depicts continent as similar size to Greenland</p><p>The United Nations has voted to adopt a resolution for the world to formally phase out the traditional Mercator map of the globe in favour of one that more accurately displays Africa’s size.</p><p>In a session at its headquarters in New York, the UN general assembly officially retired the 16th-century Mercator projection in favour of one based on the more accurate 2018 Equal Earth design.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/04/un-vote-world-map-mercator-equal-earth-africa">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Claim relating to 1960 attack on hundreds of protesters part of wave of litigation over apartheid crimes in South Africa</p><p>The day dawned brightly on 21 March 1960, as residents of the South African township of Sharpeville gathered to protest against pass laws, which forced “Black, Indian and Coloured” South Africans to carry documents at all times specifying where they were allowed to be.</p><p>Abraham Mofokeng joined the march, one of dozens organised nationwide by the Pan Africanist Congress (PAC), a breakaway group from the African National Congress (ANC). “The weather was very nice, the sun was out. You could not have suspected that the day would go so horribly,” said Mofokeng, who was then a 20-year-old factory worker.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/03/victims-sue-south-african-government-sharpeville-massacre-apartheid">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/news/ng-interactive/2026/sep/06/tupac-shakur-murder-investigation</link>
      <description><p>Police received information nearly immediately after the killing. It took Las Vegas police 27 years to make an arrest</p><p>For years, US law enforcement officials blamed their failure to solve hip-hop star <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/music/2pac">Tupac Shakur</a>’s murder on the lack of cooperation from key witnesses, and on gang members’ “snitches get stitches” culture.</p><p>But testimony in a much-delayed murder trial, which <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/music/2026/aug/31/tupac-shakur-killing-duane-keith-davis">concluded this week</a>, almost 30 years after Shakur’s death, highlighted just how much law enforcement officials knew about the shooting, and how early.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/news/ng-interactive/2026/sep/06/tupac-shakur-murder-investigation">Continue reading...</a></description>
